newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to support EU in WTO panel on Helms-Burton.
newsitem.headline: Canada to support EU in WTO panel on Helms-Burton.

text.p: Canadian International Trade Minister Art Eggleton on Thursday said Canada would support the European Union (EU) in its World Trade Organization (WTO) complaint against the controversial U.S. Helms-Burton law.

"Opposing the (Helms-Burton) Act in concert with the EU and other major trade partners sends a strong message that the international community does not accept Helms-Burton," Eggleton said in a statement.

On Wednesday the WTO agreed to a EU request to set up a panel to determine whether the Helms-Burton law violates WTO rules. The law, named after its Congressional sponsors, punishes foreign investors for doing business in Cuba.

Under Helms-Burton, U.S. citizens and companies can sue foreign investors in Cuba who use property confiscated after the 1959 communist revolution led by Fidel Castro. Executives and shareholders of foreign companies investing in the Caribbean island, as well as their families, can be denied entry into the United States.
As a third party in the EU complaint, Canada would have the right to make written and oral submissions to the WTO panel. The panel must reflect these submissions in its final report.

Although U.S. President Bill Clinton suspended the Helms-Burton provision allowing Americans to file lawsuits until sometime in January, Canada passed its own legislation in retaliation to the law. It allows Canadians to countersue in Canadian courts to recover damages awarded by U.S. courts under Helms-Burton.
Together with Mexico, Canada has also challenged the U.S. law under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA).
